title: Search and research services: Perplexity and Liner

opening.headline: We consider which source is more trustworthy, a search engine or an AI service with a source, based on the purpose and verification criteria of the source-based search and research service.
body: Search engines list long links, and it is up to the user to read and judge them. On the other hand, AI search services read multiple sources, provide organized answers at once, and add numbered sources throughout the answer. It's convenient, but whether you can trust it just because the source is attached is a separate issue.

In this class, we will look at the order in which Perplexity, a source-based search service, creates answers, and how Liner, which provides daily searches and paper searches, helps. Next, we explain the process of verifying sources using market trend research cases and summarize the standards for judging reliability.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the purpose of source-based search and research services
You can distinguish criteria for checking the reliability of search sources.

screens.title: Search engines and AI services: which source do you trust?
screens.lead: Let's look at the differences between entering the same question into a search engine and an AI search service. Read below and consider which one is more trustworthy.

visual.alt: A comparison scene with link list search results on the left and AI answers with number citations on the right.

paragraphs: Search engines will display a long list of links related to your question. Users open the link, read it, and decide for themselves what to believe. It takes time, but the judgment process is visible.

The AI search service reads multiple sources and provides organized answers at once. There are numbered sources throughout the answer so you can see where the content came from. As convenient as it is, users are less likely to open the link directly.
If so, can I trust it if there is a numbered source? This class starts from this question.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Is the fact that the source is attached proof that the content is correct, or is it a sign that the way to verify it is open? You will be able to answer this question at the end of the lesson.

screens.outro: First, let me recall my experience opening the source.

screens.title: Experience with opening the source
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Have you ever opened and checked the answer with the source directly?
items.answer: Not many people have the habit of opening it. Because if it has a number on it, it feels like it's already been confirmed. However, the number is only a starting point for verification.

items.prompt: When you opened it, was there a time when the content was different or did not open?
items.answer: There may be cases where the argument in the answer is not found in the linked article, reflects only part of the article, or access is blocked. When such cases are encountered, the claims should be treated as unconfirmed.

items.prompt: Do you judge based on the publisher and date of the source?
items.answer: The same claim has different weight depending on who made it and when. Errors spread if you use old data as if it were the current situation or use secondary sources that quote other articles as the basis. The examples in this lesson address this point specifically.

screens.outro: Let’s check out how source-based search creates answers with Perplexity.

screens.title: Perplexity: Source-based search
screens.lead: Use the arrows to the right to follow Perplexity step by step as it takes a question and provides a quoted answer.

visual.alt: Flowchart following four steps: understanding the question, searching the web, summarizing information, and providing numbered citations.
labels: Verification is up to the user

steps.title: Step 1: Understand the question
steps.body: Perplexity goes beyond simple keyword searches and uses language models to understand the context and nuance of questions. Interpreting what is being asked is the first step.

steps.title: Step 2: Search the web
steps.body: After interpreting the question, it searches the Internet in real time to gather information from sources such as articles, websites, and academic journals. The quality of the answer varies depending on which sources are gathered.

steps.title: Step 3: Summarize the information
steps.body: Organize the most relevant information you've gathered into one easy-to-understand answer. At this stage, content from multiple sources is mixed, so it becomes important which sentence comes from which source.

steps.title: Step 4: Add number citations
steps.body: Each answer is accompanied by a numbered citation linking to the original source. This number allows users to check the content directly or explore further.

steps.title: Pro Search and Deep Research
steps.body: Pro Search lets you do deeper research across multiple sources and choose models to apply to your answers. Deep Research involves repeatedly searching, reading documents, inferring what to do next, revising the research plan, and writing a report summarizing the results. The completed report can be exported as a PDF or document, or created as a page and shared.

steps.title: Verification is up to the user
steps.body: Having a citation means that the path to verification is open. Verification itself is not automatic. It's up to you to press a number to open it and decide if it matches the claim.

screens.outro: Now that you understand the search flow, let’s take a look at Liner with its research-focused features.

screens.title: Liner and paper search, source reliability criteria
screens.lead: Select each tab to check out Liner's two services and the criteria for checking source reliability.

tabs.label: Liner
tabs.body: Liner is a service for everyday searches that helps you get accurate answers and quickly move on to fact-based tasks. You can view all quotes at once, ask follow-up questions to deepen your understanding, and unpack complex topics with mind maps. The service introduction also includes testimonials that say it is used to fact-check insights from customer reports.

tabs.label: Liner Scholar
tabs.body: Liner Scholar is a service for academic work. We introduce that we help you find and compare papers that fit the topic, reinforce papers with appropriate citations, and organize literature reviews. Its purpose is different from services for everyday searches in that it is a tool tailored to searching papers.

tabs.label: Reliability check criteria
tabs.body: Regardless of the service, the criteria for checking the source are the same. First, does the source actually exist? Second, does the original text match the argument in the answer? Third, who published the data and at what time? Checking these three things can filter out quite a few errors.

tabs.label: Something easy to miss
tabs.body: There are cases where multiple sources of answers actually cite the same article repeatedly. Even if the number appears to be large, it may not be independent evidence, so check whether the data comes from different institutions or authors. If the source material is a requote from another article, check the original text.

screens.outro: Now that we've confirmed the service and inspection standards, let's unpack the process in a market research example.

screens.title: Commentary: Source verification process for market trend research
screens.lead: The instructor explains step by step the process of verifying sources when researching market trends using AI search. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: situation
steps.body: We plan to research domestic beverage market trends using AI search and include them in a report. The answer is organized into three paragraphs, and each sentence is numbered.

steps.title: Step 1: Indicate key arguments and citation numbers
steps.body: Pick three key claims to make in your report and indicate which citation number you rely on for each. When it is difficult to check everything, we first check the claims that affect the report's conclusions.

steps.title: Step 2: Open the link to see if the claim is actually written
steps.body: Open the cited link directly to check whether the answer's argument is actually written in the original text. If it does not open or contains no content, the claim is marked as unconfirmed. Citations generated by search or research functions are no exception.

steps.title: Step 3: Confirm issuing agency and date
steps.body: We check the institution and date of the original text to identify old data and secondary citations. Avoid using numbers from several years ago as a proxy for current market conditions.

steps.title: Step 4: Cross-check important numbers
steps.body: Key figures in the report, such as market size or growth rate, are cross-checked by at least two independent sources. Check whether the two sources are pointing to the same data.

steps.title: Instructor's judgment
steps.body: Each claim is labeled Confirmed, Unconfirmed, or Outdated. In the report, only confirmed claims are written, and unconfirmed items are marked or omitted. The research function only creates a draft report, and it is up to you to check the evidence. This procedure can be used not only for AI searches but also when receiving summarized data organized by humans.

screens.outro: Now that we have completed the source verification process, we will organize them into one standard.

screens.title: Just because the source is attached doesn't mean it's true.
screens.lead: We will organize what we have seen so far into one standard. Read on to recall the research I recently conducted. The last sentence will serve as a standard for future research results.

paragraphs: Source-based searches provide organized answers with links to evidence. Perplexity understands the question, searches the web, summarizes it, and adds numbered citations. Deep Research repeats this process and compiles it into a report. Liner helps you split your day-to-day searches and paper navigation.

But just because a source is attached doesn't mean it's true. The number is only a path to check, and you must open it and judge for yourself whether the contents are correct. The three basic steps are to open it, look at the publisher and date, and cross-check important figures.

The research function does not replace human judgment. It's safe to assume that at the expense of saving time-consuming navigation, you'll have more time to spend on verification. A good way to check is to ask the same question to both services and compare whether the cited sources overlap. If the sources do not overlap, open and compare to see which one you find more reliable.

callout.label: something to remember
callout.text: A source is something you verify, not something you believe in. In your report, write only verified claims.

glossary.def: This is a method that searches the web, creates an answer, and shows a link to the original text based on the answer.
It is an AI search service that provides interactive answers to questions with number quotations. We offer Pro Search and Deep Research.
It is an AI search and research service that helps check citations and search for academic papers.
It involves verifying the claims of one source with another, independent source.

misconceptions.myth: If there is a citation number, it has been verified.
misconceptions.fact: The number is only a confirmation path. You must open the link and see for yourself whether the content is true to its claims.

misconceptions.myth: AI search always provides the latest information.
misconceptions.fact: Even if you search the web in real time, it depends on what sources you gather. You should check the publication date.

misconceptions.myth: The research function replaces human judgment.
misconceptions.fact: The research function only creates a draft report. It is up to the user to check the evidence and decide the conclusion.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Source-based searches provide answers with links to evidence.
Just because a source is attached doesn't mean it's true.
Open it yourself, check the publisher and date, and cross-check important figures.
The research function creates the draft and the judgment is made by humans.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: In my recent research, what sources did I skip over without opening?

checks.q: AI search answers include number citations. What best fits what this quote means?
options: This means that the path to be verified is open, and the verification must be done by the user.
Since there is a quotation, the answer is confirmed as fact.
The more citation numbers, the more accurate the answer.
The results are exactly the same as the search engine link list.
checks.explain: Citations open a path to verification, but it is up to the user to open them and determine if they are true to the claim.

wrong.1: Just because a source is attached doesn't mean it's true.
wrong.2: The same source may be cited repeatedly, so the number alone does not indicate reliability.
wrong.3: AI search differs from link lists in that it reads multiple sources to provide an organized answer.

checks.intro: Check out for yourself the features of source-based search you just saw. Results are not recorded, and commentary appears immediately after you select an option.

checks.q: Put the process of verifying the source of market trend research answers in order.
items: Indicate key arguments and each citation number
Open the cited link to see if the claim is actually written.
Check the publishing organization and date to identify old data or secondary citations.
Cross-check important figures with two or more independent sources
checks.explain: The flow is to mark a claim, check the original text, check reliability, and finally cross-check.
checks.intro: Think of the procedure for checking sources and arrange them in order. Results are not recorded.
